title: Hymnals
hookLine: the book in the pew held a people's theology

lines: A SLOT IN THE BACK OF THE PEW.
A GRANDMOTHER SINGS IT FROM MEMORY.
cards: The pew in front of you has a slot cut into its back. In it, a thick book with a cracked spine and a faded cloth cover. Somebody's pencil has marked a page; a funeral program is tucked in at another.
Every page has lines of music above the words. Nobody would call it a theology book. It has no arguments, no footnotes.
And yet a grandmother who never read a word of theology can sing half of it from memory, and in those songs is much of what her church believes about God, sin, grace and heaven.

teach.h: THEY SANG A HYMN, AND WENT OUT.
teach.b: Start with the Gospels. After the last supper, Matthew says, "And when they had sung an hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives." Jesus's last evening with his friends ends with a song.
In Acts, Paul and Silas sit in prison, feet in the stocks: "And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them." Next, why sing at all.

Paul writes to the Colossians: "Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord."
Singing sits under teaching. A hymn is a lesson that gets into your memory through the back door. Then, the book.
A hymnal gathers what a church wants its people to carry, so it tells you what that church holds dear.

teach.h: A MIGHTY FORTRESS IS OUR GOD.
teach.b: Martin Luther's hymn, in one old English version, opens: "A mighty fortress is our God, a bulwark never failing." A whole teaching about trust, in one line you can sing on the way home. Not every church uses a hymnal.
Orthodox churches sing hymns from their service books, and some newer churches put the words up on a screen. The habit underneath is the same.
Last, Isaac Watts, whom you met back on day one hundred thirty-six: "When I survey the wondrous cross, on which the Prince of glory died."
The Prince of glory, dying: a whole doctrine about who was on the cross, sung without a footnote. That's the hymnal's quiet job.

how: In Protestant and Catholic churches a hymnal often sits in the pews and the congregation sings from it together; Orthodox churches sing hymns from their service books, and some newer churches project the words on a screen instead.

o: a book of a church's songs, words set over music
a list of the Bible readings set for each Sunday
a book of prayers said aloud by the minister alone

s: the New Testament never mentions singing hymns
Matthew says Jesus and his friends sang a hymn after supper, and Paul and Silas sang in prison.
"teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs."
every church sings from a hymnal in the pew

games.q: the last supper is over. before Jesus and his friends go out to the mount of Olives, what does Matthew say they do?
games.why: "and when they had sung an hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives." the last evening ends with a song.

practice: Read the verse on the screen, or a hymn you love, slowly, the way you'd read a letter. Then read it again, asking of each line: what does this say about God?
If you pray, you can let the last line be your prayer; if you don't, notice which line you'd remember tomorrow, and why.

wordCard.voice: Hymnals. The book of a church's songs, and of what it believes, carried in memory more than on a shelf.

orig.note: Greek: a song of praise. Colossians names hymns alongside psalms and spiritual songs.

carryVoice: Your line: theology in song. What a church sings, its people tend to carry home. Until tomorrow.
